problems: The mechanic's flat cap reads as a tall rectangular block in the render. The plain chest slab provides little period tailoring.
The clerk reads as a contemporary plain sweater and straight skirt. The small hairpin and edge-on ledger cannot carry the Industrial identity at stream scale.
The messenger's diagonal strap descends to the opposite hip from the satchel. The short cape contributes little visible shoulder silhouette, leaving a generic courier outfit.
The clerk's skirt and provisioner's apron are solid hip-bound boxes covering both legs. They need movement clearance rather than behaving as rigid boards across independently animated limbs.

The railway baron reads as another well-dressed resident, not clearly a visiting railway magnate. The watch chain and lapel badge are too small to establish that role; the rendered gold-toned bowler and pinkish coat also weaken the intended dark-hat/cream-duster contrast.

OVERALL: three of the four everyday kits are still today's shirt-and-trousers with a hat and a held box on top. At stream scale the mechanic and the messenger read as a modern workman in dungarees and a modern postman or policeman. The industrial-age markers are missing from the silhouettes: waistcoats with watch chains, braces, neckerchiefs, high collars, puffed sleeves, bustles and shawls.

OVERALL: the head and the leader are built the same way (torso box, two coat-skirt boxes, lapels, waistcoat panel). Apart from colour and hat they share one silhouette, and nothing on the leader says 'from far away'.

OVERALL: the kits use colour roles for garments the bible gives a fixed material. The heavy boots, the leader's cream coat, the leather gloves and the bowler all take the wearer's colours. In the render this gives tan 'boots' that merge with tan trousers, blue gloves, a pinkish coat and a mustard 'bowler'.
Workshop Mechanic: the cap reads as a tall square block or fez over the brow, not a flat cap. The 0.045 brim at z 0.19 hardly shows past the face and the crown has no forward slope.

Workshop Mechanic: the 'waistcoat' (hips box y 0.27, 0.47x0.49, accent:dark) is a full slab from waist to chest. It reads as dungarees or a bib apron. The shirt:light patch at y 0.505 floats below the neckline like a name badge.

Workshop Mechanic: the 'heavy boots' are pants:dark boxes from the knee down. They read as wide trouser hems (see the tan-trousered second wearer), not boots. The grey tool case reads as a modern plastic toolbox.
Municipal Clerk: the ledger (armL box 0.09 wide x 0.30 x 0.25 deep) is held edge-on to the camera and renders as a thin dark sliver, so the role prop is invisible.

Municipal Clerk: the jacket is one shirt-coloured block (0.465x0.63) over a straight column skirt: no waist, no shoulder puff, no high collar, no bustle. It reads as a jumper over a tube skirt, not a Victorian fitted jacket. The base hair plus bun renders as a blocky helmet on the crown.

Market Provisioner: the broad hat and long apron work and are the strongest everyday silhouette. But the brown box with a cream label in the hand reads as a parcel or suitcase, not a market basket. The red/green shirt-coloured pocket square on the apron looks like a sticker.

Telegraph Messenger: the 'short shoulder cape' is on the cape bone only (behind the back at z -0.035). From the front and at 40 degrees it is almost invisible, so the kit loses its one silhouette feature.

Telegraph Messenger: the satchel strap (rotation z -0.55) ends at the figure's right hip, but the satchel sits on the left hip at x 0.24. Strap and bag do not meet, and the strap reads as a stick across the chest. The satchel (x 0.16..0.32) also overlaps the left arm (inner edge x 0.23) and will clip through it as the arm swings.

Alderman (head): the top hat is excellent and reads instantly. But the waistcoat panel is 'accent', which on this wearer is gold, so the brass chain, the brass shoulder blocks and the medallion merge into one gold breastplate or harness. It does not read as a chain of office. The thick 0.065 straight bars plus the 0.17-deep brass shoulder blocks look like a yoke or epaulettes.

Alderman (head): the frock coat (shirt:dark) and trousers (pants:dark) are role colours. On this wearer they are both black and merge into one mass, and on another head the coat could come out red or green. The 'polished boots' do not exist: the leg boxes are trouser-coloured.
Alderman (head): the charter is a 0.43 m horizontal scroll centred on the right hand. Its inner end reaches hips x ≈ -0.08 and pushes through the coat front.

Railway Baron (leader): the 'bowler' is a 0.33x0.29 hat:dark sphere. In this render it is mustard with a dark band and reads as a pith helmet or miner's helmet, not a bowler. The cream coat is shirt:light and came out dusty pink. The lapels are the same colour as the coat and vanish.

Railway Baron (leader): the gloves are pants:dark (blue here). The watch chain (0.024 thick) and the crest badge are invisible at stream scale. The concession map is a flat sheet hanging at the thigh that will sweep through the leg and coat skirt when walking. The leader has no shape that reads as 'travelled far'.
fix:
Workshop Mechanic: Rebuild the cap as a shallow, forward-sloping crown with a short projecting peak; prevent underlying hair from producing a tall square silhouette. Replace the blank chest slab with a fitted work waistcoat, an exposed pale shirt collar, and a chunky button placket. Keep the rolled cuffs and dark tool case.
Municipal Clerk: Add a conspicuous pale standing collar and shaped, buttoned bodice with slightly fuller upper sleeves. Replace the solid skirt block with a subtly flared, hollow or panelled skirt that clears the legs during walking. Make the rear bun larger and seat it against the hair; angle the ledger outward so its broad cover is visible from above.
Market Provisioner: Retain the broad hat and contrasting canvas apron. Fit the bib against the torso, make its supporting straps explicit, and replace the deep rigid lower box with a thin hanging apron panel with gait clearance. Give the carried parcel an unmistakable hamper or provision-basket silhouette rather than another small tool case.
Telegraph Messenger: Reverse the diagonal strap's Z rotation from -0.55 to approximately +0.55 and adjust its lower end to meet the satchel's actual attachment point. Add a standing tunic collar and a few oversized brass fastenings. Shape the cape around the upper back with separate shoulder pieces that follow the arms, rather than one slab bridging them. Preserve a taller cylindrical cap crown to distinguish it from the mechanic's shallow cap.
Alderman: Preserve the tall black top hat, dark formal coat, broad brass collar, and large medallion. These already establish rank effectively. Check coat-tail clearance in a walking pose and ensure the charter is visibly gripped rather than hovering beside the hand.
Railway Baron: Lock the bowler to charcoal and the travel coat to warm cream rather than inherited avatar colours. Give the coat a distinctive contrasting storm yoke and generous travel lapels. Add a chunky brass-cornered portmanteau with a large railway-company emblem visible on its upper face; simplify the map into a bold route graphic. Use these large travel cues, not the tiny watch chain and pin, to establish the visiting railway magnate. / GENERAL: give each kit one big period shape the others lack. Use fixed colours for the materials the bible names: leather boots and gloves #42494c or #8b6245, brass #b8914e, cream #d3c7aa, office black #263f40. Keep roles for the cloth that should stay personal.

WORKSHOP MECHANIC
- Cap: a real flat cap. Crown box [0,0.335,0.02] size [0.37,0.07,0.36] with rotation x 0.15 so it slopes forward. Peak box [0,0.30,0.20] size [0.32,0.035,0.14].
- Waistcoat: replace the slab with a short open waistcoat on the hips bone. Two front panels, each [0.17,0.36,0.03] at x ±0.12, y 0.34, z 0.145, in accent:dark, leaving a shirt:light V gap down the middle. Add three brass button cubes 0.03 on one panel and a brass watch-chain bar.
- Neck: drop the floating collar patch. Add a neckerchief, a red #d9534f box [0.22,0.08,0.05] at y 0.58, z 0.13.
- Boots: fixed #42494c boxes [0.22,0.26,0.27] at [0,-0.67,0.04], with a thicker toe box. The trousers then stop visibly at the boot top.
- Tool case: brown #8b6245 wooden carpenter's tray, an open box [0.30,0.10,0.14] with a dowel handle above it in #b8914e.

MUNICIPAL CLERK
- Ledger: hold it face-on. armL box [0.03,0.30,0.22] rotated y 1.5708 so the cover faces +z, or carry it against the chest on the hips bone at [0.08,0.25,0.17] size [0.22,0.28,0.05], in #263f40 with a #d3c7aa page edge.
- Jacket: give it period shape.
  - Leg-of-mutton puffs: shirt spheres [0.2,0.18,0.2] at the top of each arm (y -0.05).
  - High collar band: shirt:dark [0.26,0.08,0.24] at y 0.6.
  - Waist belt: accent:dark [0.46,0.05,0.3] at y 0.12.
  - Peplum flare: shirt [0.5,0.1,0.34] at y 0.03.
- Skirt: flare the hem with a second box [0.6,0.14,0.42] at y -0.70. Add a bustle, pants:dark [0.36,0.24,0.18] at [0,-0.05,-0.2].
- Hair: show the face edge. Use a smaller bun sphere at [0,0.33,-0.12] and do not cover the brow.

MARKET PROVISIONER
- Keep the hat and apron.
- Basket: replace the parcel with an open wicker basket. Body #b8914e box [0.30,0.14,0.20] with an arched handle (two thin uprights plus a bar, all on armL). Show produce in it: two or three spheres in #596f52 and #d9534f poking above the rim.
- Pocket: make the apron pocket the same apron colour, one shade darker (shirt:light, so it does not read as a sticker).
- Optional: a shawl crossed over the bib, accent [0.5,0.12,0.32] at y 0.5, for an extra period cue.

TELEGRAPH MESSENGER
- Cape: make it read from the front. A pelerine on the hips bone, shirt:dark box [0.58,0.20,0.36] at [0,0.47,0], wider than the shoulders. Keep the back cape but lengthen it to 0.45.
- Jacket: short and double-breasted, with two vertical rows of three brass #b8914e cubes at x ±0.07 on the chest.
- Cap: add a chin strap, a thin #42494c box under the jaw.
- Satchel: move it to the figure's right hip so it sits clear of the arm, at [-0.20,0.02,0.14] size [0.20,0.22,0.08] on the hips bone. Run the strap from the left shoulder (rotation z +0.55, thinner, 0.045 wide) so it meets the bag.
- Trousers: tuck them into knee-high socks or gaiters (legs #a7a397 below the knee) for a knickerbocker youth silhouette, so the kit differs from the mechanic's.

ALDERMAN (HEAD)
- Keep the top hat.
- Colours: frock coat fixed #263f40, trousers #42494c with a separate polished-boot box in near-black #1f2426 and a light toe highlight. Waistcoat fixed claret #d9534f-darkened or #a7a397, never accent/gold, so the brass contrasts.
- Chain: rebuild as a chain of links. A U of 7 to 9 small #b8914e cubes (0.06) draped from each shoulder to a low point at y 0.3. Remove the brass shoulder blocks. Make the medallion bigger and lower: cylinder [0.22,0.04,0.22] at y 0.24, with a #f2cf83 inner disc.
- Charter: hold it vertically, armR cylinder [0.09,0.40,0.09] with no rotation at [0,-0.55,0.08], so it does not pass through the coat.

RAILWAY BARON (LEADER)
- Bowler: fixed #42494c. Lower, rounder crown, sphere [0.31,0.20,0.29] at y 0.40. Narrow brim, cylinder [0.40,0.03,0.36] at y 0.32.
- Coat: fixed #d3c7aa. Lapels in #a7a397 so they show.
- Far-travel silhouette: add an Inverness shoulder cape on the cape bone plus a front hips-bone capelet [0.6,0.24,0.38] at y 0.44 in a #c27f59 check-brown. This wide shoulder line is what tells him from the Alderman at a distance.
- Gloves: fixed #8b6245.
- Watch chain: double its thickness to 0.04 or drop it.
- Second prop: in the left hand, a leather Gladstone bag #8b6245 [0.30,0.20,0.14] with a brass clasp, and a label patch in #83b6bd/#f2cf83 sized 0.1 or more so the 'foreign trunk label' reads.
- Map: shrink it to a rolled tube held vertically in the right hand (cylinder [0.08,0.42,0.08]) so it never sweeps through the leg.
